page: Testing Helper for testing Hono applications. Import: {Hono} from 'hono', {testClient} from 'hono/testing'. Function: testClient(app) returns typed client for testing. Type-safe routing: must use chained methods directly on new Hono(). Pattern: new Hono().get(...).post(...) not separate app.get(). Client methods: .$get(), .$post(), .$put(), .$delete() etc. Parameters: query, body, params objects. Second parameter: headers and RequestInit options. Response: has status, json(), text() like fetch Response. Example: client.search.$get({query: {q: 'hono'}}) calls GET /search?q=hono. Headers: pass as second parameter with Authorization, Content-Type. Assertions: expect res.status, expect await res.json(). Type inference: requires chained method definition for autocompletion. Questions: How to test? Type safety? Chained methods? Headers? Response handling? Query params?

testClient() function for creating typed test clients. Signature: testClient(app) returns typed client matching app routes. Type safety: requires chained method definition. Pattern: const app = new Hono().get(...).post(...). Returns: object with method functions like .$get(), .$post(). Usage: const client = testClient(app). Method calls: await client.search.$get({query: {q: 'hono'}}). Response: {status, json(), text()} like fetch Response. Example: client.endpoint.$get(params, {headers: {...}}). Questions: Setup? Chained methods? Type safety? Method calls? Response?

Type inference requirement for testClient. Must use chained methods on Hono instance. Works: const app = new Hono().get('/search', handler). Doesn't work: const app = new Hono(); app.get('/search', handler). Chaining required: type info flows through .get/.post/etc calls. Separate definition: loses type information. Pattern: all routes chained for full type safety. Autocompletion: depends on chaining. Questions: Why chaining? Type inference? Autocompletion? Separate routes?

testClient parameters and headers. First parameter: route params like {query: {q: 'hono'}} for query strings. Second parameter: init object with headers, method, body. Headers example: {Authorization: `Bearer ${token}`, 'Content-Type': 'application/json'}. RequestInit options: full fetch RequestInit support. Method override: can set custom method. Body: can include request body. Assertions: expect res.status, expect await res.json(), expect await res.text(). Questions: Query params? Headers? Body? Methods? Assertions?
